fine_trace.note: ASan reports an 8-byte out-of-bounds WRITE when n_headers reaches the fixed header_start capacity.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The attacker controls the HTTP request header layout, including CR-delimited header lines. parse_headers stores each header as a start/end pointer pair in a fixed header_start array. The vulnerable code writes header_start[n_headers++] before checking capacity, and the later check uses n_headers > N_HEADER_START rather than n_headers >= N_HEADER_START. A request with enough header fragments can therefore write index N_HEADER_START before the parser rejects the input, producing the observed global-buffer-overflow write.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch rejects too-short header lines before storing them, and changes the capacity guard to `n_headers >= N_HEADER_START`. This prevents the parser from writing a start/end pair when the fixed header_start array is full.
